q-339135.name: Question 1
q-339135.worked_solution:
Let's sketch the graph of $y=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(x):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14189988/assets/24f07da42a537ded7916fc2440dcf3ee1ccdfc81c7b027b47e97814fec059f5a.png)

The domain of $\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(x)$ is $x\in [-1,1].$  

Now, substituting $x=0$ directly into the limit, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,0}\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(x)+6}{2x+3} & =\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(0)+6}{2(0)+3} \\  & =\frac{6}{3} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

q-339125.name: Question 2
q-339125.worked_solution:
Let's sketch the graph of $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14189988/assets/ca5e8035505f20619b6707d6d1f2d0b7b2f125a004a0dbd9d448840b0e4ffd99.png)

The domain of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)$ is $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

Now, substituting $x=0$ directly into the limit, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,0}\frac{7\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)}{{x}^{2}+5} & =\frac{7\operatorname{arctan}⁡(0)}{(0)^{2}+5} \\  & =\frac{7(0)}{5} \\  & =\frac{0}{5} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-152787.name: Question 3
q-152787.worked_solution:
Let's sketch the graph of $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14189988/assets/fc06a4e63f38a315dd3944f65f871cca2dbdddee26ec268e857f79e5f4ab8848.png)

The domain of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)$ is $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

Now, substituting $x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ directly into the limit, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,\sqrt{3}/3}(12\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)+\pi ) & =12\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})+\pi  \\  & =12\cdot \frac{\pi }{6}+\pi  \\  & =3\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

q-344536.name: Question 6
q-344536.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch the graph of $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x+1):$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14189988/assets/4d81187377609f2cc79f2f972b1416a00f854d8c7a72731eb306aaa17d9f7339.png)

The domain of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x+1)$ is $(-\infty ,\infty ).$ Moreover, from the graph, we see that

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x+1)=-\frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-\infty }\frac{2}{\pi }\,(\frac{\pi }{2}-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x+1))=\frac{2}{\pi }\,(\frac{\pi }{2}-(-\frac{\pi }{2}))=2.
$$

q-152891.name: Question 11
q-152891.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch the graph of  $y=\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}}):$   

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14189988/assets/4abceba56f404b0b39fbde4b1f7da0ec36e69a496c4ef52d3bebfbcb8c7d3380.png)

The domain of   $\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}})$ is $(-\infty ,\infty ).$    

Now, substituting $x=3$ directly into the limit, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}})) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}})) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3})) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-302680.name: Question 12
q-302680.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14189988/assets/24f07da42a537ded7916fc2440dcf3ee1ccdfc81c7b027b47e97814fec059f5a.png)

 

The domain of $\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(x)$ is $x\in [-1,1].$  

Now, substituting $x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ directly into the limit, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,\sqrt{3}/2}\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(x)) & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3}{4}\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})) \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{3}{4}\cdot \frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-302690.name: Question 13
q-302690.worked_solution:
Let's sketch the graph of $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14189988/assets/fc06a4e63f38a315dd3944f65f871cca2dbdddee26ec268e857f79e5f4ab8848.png)

The domain of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)$ is $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

As $x$ increases to $\infty ,$ the graph tends to $y=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,\infty }\operatorname{tan}⁡(4\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)) & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡(2\pi ) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-152890.name: Question 14
q-152890.worked_solution:
Let's sketch the graph of $y=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14189988/assets/ca5e8035505f20619b6707d6d1f2d0b7b2f125a004a0dbd9d448840b0e4ffd99.png)

The domain of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)$ is $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

As $x$ increases to $\infty ,$ the graph tends to $y=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,\infty }\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(x)) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
